item.title: Reports: Bears QB Tyson Bagent to start vs. Jets
item.description: Chicago Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent is expected to start Sunday's game against the visiting New York Jets, multiple outlets reported on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chicago Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent is expected to start Sunday's game against the visiting New York Jets, multiple outlets reported on Saturday. Bagent took the majority of the first-team reps at practice this week. He gets the nod over Case Keenum, who passed for 247 yards and accounted for three touchdowns (two passing, one rushing) in Monday night's 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles after Bagent spent much of the previous week in concussion protocol. Bagent was injured late in the fourth quarter of Chicago's 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 20. He came on in relief of Caleb Williams, who sustained a Grade 2 hamstring strain in that game. Williams has been ruled out for the Bears (2-1) on Sunday against the Jets (1-2). Bagent earned the No. 2 role in training camp but said earlier this week he was not pushing to unseat Keenum, who was given a game ball Monday night. "There's a couple ways to think about it. Obviously, I would like everything that the football world can offer me. But then there's also the part that I am from Shepherd University, so I have absolutely zero ego in this and nobody is a bigger cheerleader and a fan of Case Keenum than I am," Bagent said. "I think he is the epitome of what I believe a quarterback is and is supposed to be. So it was fun to watch him play." Asked on Friday, Bears head coach Ben Johnson did not reveal his QB1 plans. "We'll find out on Sunday," he said. "I know both of them are well prepared to play and win a game for us." Bagent, 26, last started an NFL game during the 2023 season. He went 2-2 in place of former Bears quarterback Justin Fields. In 13 career games, Bagent has completed 65.8% of his passes for 971 yards with three touchdowns and six interceptions. --Field Level Media

item.title: Padres' Walker Buehler begins NLDS on paternity leave
item.description: Major League Baseball announced Saturday that San Diego Padres right-hander Walker Buehler has been placed on the postseason paternity list.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Major League Baseball announced Saturday that San Diego Padres right-hander Walker Buehler has been placed on the postseason paternity list. During the two-time All-Star's absence, right-hander Randy Vasquez will be on the active roster for the National League Division Series against the Brewers, which begins Saturday night in Milwaukee. Buehler, 32, is permitted to be away from the Padres for one to three days. Upon his return, he will replace Vazquez on the NLDS roster. "Exciting time for him and his wife to be having a baby this weekend, happens to be during the Division Series, which is exciting," San Diego manager Craig Stammen said prior to Game 1. "Don't have any word on what's going on yet but it could happen at any moment. I'm sure there will be stuff that comes out when it does happen. But excited for the Buehler family." Game 1 of the best-of-five series would have been Buehler's turn in the rotation. He held the Brewers to one run on three hits in six innings in an 11-2 victory in San Diego on Aug. 11. Game 2 is Sunday in Milwaukee. The earliest Buehler can pitch is Game 3 when the series shifts to San Diego on Tuesday night. Left-hander Robbie Ray is the Padres' scheduled starter for Game 1, followed by right-hander Michael King for Game 2. Ray will be opposed by hard-throwing right-hander Jacob Misiorowski (16-5, 1.80 ERA), who leads the majors in ERA and strikeouts (252 in 174 2/3 innings). Buehler's wife, McKenzie, is expected to give birth to their second child on Saturday, according to the San Diego Union-Tribune. Their daughter, Finley, was born in January 2024. Buehler stayed behind in San Diego when the club traveled to Milwaukee. "I think we didn't want Walker having to pitch on a possible day of the birth of his child and miss that," Stammen said. "I think it made sense that he's able to stay in San Diego and allow that to happen and not having to worry about pitching and that going on at the same time." Buehler was 9-6 with a 4.63 ERA in 32 starts in his first season with the Padres. A two-time World Series champion with the Los Angeles Dodgers, Buehler did not pitch in the NL wild-card sweep against the Chicago Cubs. He is 4-4 with a 3.04 ERA in 19 appearances (18 starts) in the postseason. Vasquez, 27, was 10-6 with a 3.90 ERA in 32 games (23 starts) this season for San Diego. --Field Level Media

item.title: Pirata informático de ShinyHunters, implicado en robo de datos del FBI, detenido en Jordania: fuentes
item.description: Un presunto miembro del grupo de piratas informáticos ShinyHunters, que afirma haber robado datos de todos los empleados del FBI, fue detenido esta semana en Jordania y está cooperando con la agencia de investigación, informaron a Reuters tres personas familiarizadas con el asunto.
item.dc:creator: Jana Winter, Raphael Satter, A.J. Vicens
item.content:encoded: Un presunto miembro del grupo de piratas informáticos ShinyHunters, que afirma haber robado datos de todos los empleados del FBI, fue detenido esta semana en Jordania y está cooperando con la agencia de investigación, informaron a Reuters tres personas familiarizadas con el asunto. Saif al-Din Khader fue detenido por las autoridades jordanas, según las tres fuentes. Dos de ellas afirmaron que fue puesto bajo custodia el martes. Reuters no pudo determinar de inmediato las circunstancias de la detención de Khader ni el lugar donde se encuentra recluido. Dos fuentes señalaron que está colaborando con el FBI y las fuerzas del orden internacionales para localizar a los demás hackers del grupo. El FBI se negó a hacer comentarios sobre ninguna detención o actividad concreta en el extranjero, pero dijo que la agencia "sigue investigando de forma enérgica el reciente incidente cibernético en el que presuntamente están implicados los ShinyHunters, habiendo colaborado ya con sus socios para detener a varios sospechosos, y no escatimaremos recursos para llevar ante la justicia a cada uno de los responsables". Los intentos de Reuters por contactar con Khader y con miembros de su familia durante la última semana y media han sido infructuosos. La detención de Khader, cuyo supuesto apodo de hacker es Rey, supone un nuevo giro en el caso de ShinyHunters. Los expertos creen que este prolífico grupo de ciberchantaje, que cuenta con un largo historial de ataques contra grandes empresas de todo el mundo, está formado principalmente por jóvenes hackers angloparlantes especializados en el robo de datos y la extorsión. Su robo de lo que, según afirman, son montañas de datos sobre todos y cada uno de los empleados del FBI ha suscitado comparaciones con la intrusión, presuntamente vinculada a China, en la Oficina de Gestión de Personal de Estados Unidos en 2015, que puso en peligro datos confidenciales de millones de estadounidenses que habían sido sometidos a controles de seguridad. INFORMACIÓN SENSIBLE Un análisis de Reuters de una muestra de los datos compartidos por ShinyHunters reveló que estos contenían una gran cantidad de información de identificación personal de los empleados del FBI, datos confidenciales sobre sus funciones laborales e información psiquiátrica y médica. La cooperación de Khader con los investigadores podría ser fundamental para ayudar a contener, o al menos comprender, el daño. Una fuente dijo que estaba guiando a los investigadores a través de sus dispositivos electrónicos y su correspondencia digital para ayudar al FBI a localizar a sus cómplices. "Su cooperación es fundamental para los esfuerzos en curso destinados a detener a estos hackers", dijo la fuente a Reuters. Desde hace días había indicios de que ShinyHunters estaba sufriendo trastornos tras el anuncio de su intrusión en el FBI. A partir del martes, Reuters no pudo ponerse en contacto con ShinyHunters a través de la cuenta en línea que utilizaba anteriormente para comunicarse con los periodistas. Posteriormente, el miércoles, desapareció el sitio web de la dark web del grupo, donde anteriormente había publicado amenazas contra el FBI. El director del FBI, Kash Patel, había insinuado que se producirían más detenciones tras el anuncio de que otro presunto miembro de ShinyHunters, Pepijn van der Stap, había sido detenido en los Países Bajos.

item.title: Sinner se retira del Masters de Shanghái debido a su lesión de rodilla
item.description: El número uno del mundo, Jannik Sinner, se retiró del Masters de Shanghái de la próxima semana, ya que sigue recuperándose de una lesión de rodilla que le ha mantenido apartado de las pistas desde que ganó el título de Wimbledon en julio.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El número uno del mundo, Jannik Sinner, se retiró del Masters de Shanghái de la próxima semana, ya que sigue recuperándose de una lesión de rodilla que le ha mantenido apartado de las pistas desde que ganó el título de Wimbledon en julio. El italiano, de 25 años, no ha jugado desde su triunfo en el All England Club, por lo que se ha perdido la gira norteamericana sobre pista dura, incluido el Abierto de Estados Unidos, y el torneo ATP 500 que se está disputando actualmente en Pekín. "Por desgracia, este año no podré jugar en el Rolex Shanghái Masters como esperaba", escribió Sinner el sábado en Instagram. "Siempre disfruto jugando ante el público de Shanghái y lamento mucho no poder hacerlo la semana que viene". El torneo Masters 1000 se celebra del 7 al 18 de octubre y cuenta con un potente cuadro encabezado por el cuatro veces campeón Novak Djokovic, junto con Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, Daniil Medvédev, Ben Shelton, Félix Auger-Aliassimey el vigente campeón, Valentin Vacherot. Sinner se alzó con el título de Shanghái en 2024, tras derrotar a Djokovic en la final. La ausencia de Sinner podría dar un impulso a las aspiraciones de Zverev de terminar la temporada como número uno del mundo. El alemán, campeón este año de Roland Garros y del Abierto de Estados Unidos, se ha convertido en el rival más cercano del italiano. Zverev puede avanzar a lo más alto de la clasificación por primera vez si gana tanto el Abierto de China en Pekín como el Masters de Shanghái.

item.title: Paris police chief says student protest movement out of control, urges peaceful action
item.description: Patrice Faure said the people who launched the movement no longer controlled it.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The student protest movement that has spread across France is now "out of control", the Paris police chief said on Saturday, urging demonstrators to return to peaceful action and warning that authorities would respond firmly to violence and vandalism. [USN:L1N45O03R TEXT:"Riot police"] clashed with high school students across France on Friday and unions called for teachers to strike as President Emmanuel Macron's government battled to contain increasingly violent protests over classroom conditions and funding. Since Monday, around 5,000 people, mostly teenagers, have been arrested nationwide and dozens injured. Agathe Foucault, a spokesperson for the national police, told RTL radio on Saturday that more than 600 police officers had also been injured. Teachers and members of the public have been attacked, while damage to property is estimated in the tens of millions of euros. Paris police chief Patrice Faure, in an open letter published on X ahead of planned renewed protests from next Tuesday, said those who had launched the movement no longer controlled it and called on students to abandon school blockades and unrest in favour of peaceful forms of protest. "It is time to return to peaceful forms of action," Faure wrote, saying parents also had a responsibility to steer their children away from what he described as the influence of "professional rioters" and their supporters. Student unions have called for a national day of demonstrations on Tuesday. Security officials fear that an organised protest in central Paris in particular could see further violence amid concerns that far-left anarchist groups could hijack the movement. [USN:L6N45M1EJ TEXT:"The students blockading"] high schools have voiced anger over overcrowding in classrooms, regular shortages of teachers and dilapidated buildings, blaming years of underinvestment.

item.title: Tennessee prison chief resigns after failed execution
item.description: The head of the Tennessee Department of Correction will step down this month, state officials said on Saturday, days after convicted murderer Christa Pike was left gravely ill from the state's failed attempt to execute her by lethal injection.
item.dc:creator: Sheila Dang
item.content:encoded: The head of the Tennessee Department of Correction will step down this month, state officials said on Saturday, days after convicted murderer Christa Pike was left gravely ill from the state's [USN:L1N45O0WH TEXT:"failed attempt to execute"] her by lethal injection. The botched execution on Wednesday left Pike unconscious, intubated and hooked to a mechanical ventilator to breathe, her lawyers wrote in a Friday court filing. It is the state's second failed execution attempt this year, prompting Tennessee Governor Bill Lee to halt attempts to carry out the death penalty for the rest of 2026. Lee said on Saturday that Frank Strada has resigned as Department of Correction commissioner and would leave his position this month. The governor had ordered an independent review of the execution attempt at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville, the state capital. Strada, in a separate statement, said that although he believes his agency's personnel followed proper protocol, "stepping aside is in the best interest of Tennesseans as the independent review moves forward." An interim commissioner will be announced later, the governor's office said. "Commissioner Strada has served with integrity, and I appreciate his willingness to put the interests of Tennesseans first during this difficult moment,” Lee said in a statement. Pike's lawyers have accused Correction Department officials of ignoring prior warnings from her doctors that her small veins and a blood disorder called thrombocytosis would make placing intravenous lines especially difficult. Pike, 50, was convicted three decades ago of first-degree murder for her role in the torture and killing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer in 1995, when Pike was 18. Doctors were working to save Pike's life and clear the drug pentobarbital from her system, her lawyers said on Friday.

item.title: Brasil vence 4-0 a India en partido amistoso, en debut goleador de Samuel Lino con la selección
item.description: Samuel Lino marcó sus dos primeros goles con la selección de Brasil, mientras que el frenético esfuerzo de la India por contener a los cinco veces campeones del mundo se desvaneció tras un comienzo enérgico, lo que permitió a los visitantes llevarse una cómoda victoria por 4-0 en un partido amistoso disputado el sábado.
item.dc:creator: Chiranjit Ojha
item.content:encoded: Samuel Lino marcó sus dos primeros goles con la selección de Brasil, mientras que el frenético esfuerzo de la India por contener a los cinco veces campeones del mundo se desvaneció tras un comienzo enérgico, lo que permitió a los visitantes llevarse una cómoda victoria por 4-0 en un partido amistoso disputado el sábado. El extremo del Chelsea Estevao marcó el primer gol de Brasil y asistió a Pedro antes de que Lino anotara un doblete en la segunda parte, lo que ayudó al equipo de Carlo Ancelotti a concluir su gira por Australia e India con dos victorias y un empate. Ancelotti, que fue probando diferentes combinaciones en la plantilla durante los tres amistosos, realizó ocho cambios respecto a la victoria del martes por 4-2 sobre Australia, manteniendo únicamente a Vinícius Jr., Danilo y Gabriel Bontempo. La estrategia de la India de dejar a Vinícius sin tanta marca por la izquierda y tenderle trampas de fuera de juego tuvo un cierto éxito inicial, ya que combinaron a sus defensas con un centro del campo bajo para contener a Brasil y buscaron al único delantero, Manvir Singh, con pases en profundidad. Pero Estevao abrió el marcador en el minuto 28, recortando desde la derecha para rematar con la izquierda al primer palo, antes de asistir en el segundo gol de Brasil con un pase que rompió la defensa y que Pedro convirtió en gol. Pedro asistió a Samuel Lino para el tercer gol cerca de la hora de juego, antes de que el extremo del Flamengo, de 26 años, regateara a dos defensas para poner el 4-0 justo antes del final del partido, mientras los 51.000 espectadores del Salt Lake Stadium animaban a los visitantes con el mismo entusiasmo que a su propia selección. India, número 138 del mundo, se quedó lamentando las ocasiones falladas, ya que Manvir y Ryan Williams no lograron marcar un gol de consuelo, prolongando además su racha sin victorias a seis partidos.

item.title: Vanderbilt QB Blaze Berlowitz to start vs. No. 2 Georgia
item.description: Vanderbilt quarterback Jared Curtis has been ruled out of Saturday's game at No. 2 Georgia in Athens due to an undisclosed injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Vanderbilt quarterback Jared Curtis has been ruled out of Saturday's game at No. 2 Georgia in Athens due to an undisclosed injury. Blaze Berlowitz will get the nod in place of Curtis, who flipped his commitment from the Bulldogs to the Commodores in December in a surprise that helped signify Vanderbilt's rise from the Southeastern Conference basement. Berlowitz has completed 14 of 25 pass attempts for 178 yards this season for the Commodores (3-1, 0-1). Curtis, 19, has thrown for 746 yards and four touchdowns with three interceptions, and he has rushed for two scores across his first four career games. --Field Level Media

item.title: Latvia PM's United List ahead in election, exit poll shows
item.description: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' centrist United List looked set to win Saturday's election for parliament, as widely expected, but must build a coalition with other parties to stay in power, an exit poll showed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' centrist United List looked set to win Saturday's election for parliament, [USN:L8N45L1R2 TEXT:"as widely expected"], but must build a coalition with other parties to stay in power, an exit poll showed. Security concerns and cost of living issues have dominated the election agenda in Latvia, a NATO and European Union member state which borders Russia and is home to a significant Russian-speaking minority.

item.description: Bloomberg Pursuits reporter Sarah Rappaport tells Bloomberg This Weekend that luxury travelers are increasingly seeking tiny hotels with as few as one to six rooms, combining the privacy of a villa with personalized high-end hotel service. item.title: Colts downgrade WR Keenan Allen to out vs. Commanders
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts ruled out Keenan Allen for Sunday's game in London against the Washington Commanders and elevated fellow wide receiver Nick Westbrook-Ikhine from the practice squad.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Indianapolis Colts ruled out Keenan Allen for Sunday's game in London against the Washington Commanders and elevated fellow wide receiver Nick Westbrook-Ikhine from the practice squad. Allen, 34, was downgraded from questionable as he nurses a groin injury. He has 13 catches for 100 yards and a touchdown this season for the Colts (1-2) after signing a one-year contract on Aug. 18. A six-time Pro Bowl selection, Allen has 1,068 career receptions for 12,151 receiving yards and 71 touchdowns in 174 games with the San Diego/Los Angeles Chargers (2013-23, 2025), Chicago Bears (2024) and Colts. Westbrook-Ikhine, 29, also was elevated from the practice squad to play in last Sunday's 19-17 victory over the Houston Texans. He joins Josh Downs, Laquon Treadwell, Deion Burks, Anthony Gould, Ashton Dulin and Darius Slayton as receivers available to play versus the Commanders (1-2). --Field Level Media

item.title: Ucrania atacará las refinerías rusas en respuesta a la "nueva doctrina" de Moscú sobre ataques aéreos
item.description: Ucrania redoblará sus ataques contra las refinerías de petróleo rusas en respuesta a una nueva política de ataques aéreos por parte de Moscú, destinada a obligar a la población a abandonar Kiev y otras ciudades, pero no atacará a civiles, dijo el presidente Volodímir Zelenski.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: Ucrania redoblará sus ataques contra las refinerías de petróleo rusas en respuesta a una nueva política de ataques aéreos por parte de Moscú, destinada a obligar a la población a abandonar Kiev y otras ciudades, pero no atacará a civiles, dijo el presidente Volodímir Zelenski. Los servicios de inteligencia ucranianos han obtenido documentos que demuestran que el líder ruso, Vladimir Putin, había emitido una "nueva doctrina" de ataques militares contra una gama mucho más amplia de objetivos civiles de cara a este invierno boreal, señaló Zelenski. "Hemos visto los documentos y sabemos que les permiten atacar infraestructuras... logística... carreteras, colegios, hospitales, para presionar a la población a que abandone la capital y otras ciudades", afirmó Zelenski. "Ese es el objetivo de la operación". Según Zelenski, lo que impulsó este cambio de política fue el deseo de Putin de aparentar fortaleza en un momento en que su ejército estaba perdiendo terreno en una región clave del frente y sufriendo un mayor número de bajas. El Kremlin no estuvo disponible para hacer declaraciones el sábado. Sin embargo, en un comunicado en el que instaba a los ciudadanos extranjeros a abandonar Kiev, el Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores ruso dijo que Moscú seguiría atacando sistemáticamente objetivos en lo que calificó de ataques de represalia por los ataques ucranianos contra Rusia en los últimos meses. Ambas partes niegan haber atacado deliberadamente a civiles. CONTRAOFENSIVA EN DOMBÁS Zelenski dijo que una contraofensiva ucraniana en curso, cuyo nombre en clave es "Vivaldi", había recuperado unos 140 km² de la región oriental ucraniana del Dombás, sobre la que Rusia ha declarado que debe ejercer un control total como condición para cualquier acuerdo de paz. En las últimas semanas, la Administración del presidente estadounidense Donald Trump ha intentado reactivar las negociaciones para poner fin al conflicto, que ya dura cuatro años y es el más sangriento de Europa desde la Segunda Guerra Mundial. El mes pasado, el líder estadounidense instó a Ucrania a abstenerse de atacar las instalaciones petroleras rusas, alegando que ello estaba provocando una subida vertiginosa de los precios mundiales del diésel. Sin embargo, Zelenski, en declaraciones realizadas mientras sonaban las sirenas antiaéreas fuera de los salones dorados de la presidencia, dijo que no había recibido ninguna señal por parte de Rusia de que Putin estuviera interesado en las negociaciones de paz ni en discutir un alto el fuego en relación con las infraestructuras energéticas. Durante la última semana, la capital ucraniana ha sido objeto de ataques persistentes por parte de drones y misiles rusos dirigidos contra activos energéticos y de telecomunicaciones, así como sobre infraestructuras viarias y ferroviarias. Por primera vez, Rusia ha atacado los puentes que cruzan el río Dniéper y conectan el este y el oeste de Kiev. Zelenski afirmó que Ucrania respondería al cambio de táctica de Moscú, pero que no respondería de la misma manera atacando indiscriminadamente infraestructuras civiles. "Tenemos que responder de cualquier forma (que podamos). Ante sus ataques contra nuestro sector energético, tenemos que responder atacando el suyo. En primer lugar, las refinerías de petróleo: lo que les proporciona los fondos para esta guerra", dijo Zelenski en inglés. "Pero, por supuesto, no responderemos, al igual que ellos, atacando objetivos civiles". APOYO DE EUROPA Después de que la Administración Trump invitara a Putin a asistir a la cumbre del G20 en Miami en diciembre y discutiera acuerdos comerciales con los enviados rusos, Zelenski instó a Washington a no normalizar las relaciones con Rusia antes de garantizar el retorno a la paz. Zelenski aseguró que estaría encantado de reunirse con Putin para mantener conversaciones de paz en el G20, pero advirtió a Estados Unidos que no se hiciera ilusiones de que Rusia pondría fin a las hostilidades si conseguía el control del Dombás. "No es justo simplemente normalizarlo", afirmó Zelenski, vestido con su característica camiseta negra y chaqueta de estilo militar. Cualquier reanudación de los lazos económicos y diplomáticos con Occidente debía ser a cambio de la paz, señaló: "Porque la paz es más importante que cualquier tipo de economía". Aunque Estados Unidos ha propuesto reanudar las conversaciones trilaterales en las próximas semanas en los Emiratos Árabes Unidos, Zelenski señaló que aún no se había fijado una fecha ni un lugar concretos para las conversaciones a nivel técnico. Las autoridades ucranianas advierten de que Rusia ha acumulado cientos de misiles balísticos de cara a una esperada ofensiva invernal frente las infraestructuras eléctricas y de agua. En el invierno boreal pasado, el más duro de la guerra, los ataques rusos dejaron amplias zonas del país sin electricidad ni calefacción durante días. Desde el verano boreal, Moscú también ha comenzado a lanzar cada día sobre Ucrania decenas de drones Shahed propulsados por reactores, rápidos y relativamente baratos, ante los que las defensas aéreas ucranianas han tenido dificultades, ya que su anterior generación de drones interceptores era demasiado lenta para alcanzarlos. Zelenski dijo que Ucrania se había visto obligada a depender en gran medida de sus aviones de combate, F-16 y MiG, para derribar alrededor del 60% de los drones rusos propulsados por reactores, pero que las reservas de munición de 20 mm para los aviones se estaban agotando. Kiev estaba trabajando con urgencia en otras soluciones, entre ellas reforzar sus capacidades de interferencia, dijo. En la segunda quincena de octubre, recibiría el primer envío de misiles de defensa aérea pequeños y económicos capaces de derribar los nuevos Shahed. La semana pasada, Zelenski dijo que Ucrania estaba desarrollando cinco modelos de nuevos drones interceptores capaces de derribar los Shahed a reacción. Tras una reunión con sus jefes de defensa, señaló que las pruebas realizadas con dos de esos modelos habían mostrado una tasa de éxito modesta, de alrededor del 30%. "Tendremos que ampliar la escala", dijo. «Espero que con todo esto, con todos estos elementos, encontremos una solución". AMENAZA BALÍSTICA Ucrania anunció esta semana el primer uso en combate de su propio misil balístico de fabricación nacional: el FP-7, que tiene un alcance de unos 250 kilómetros. Zelenski dijo que había llamado al fabricante, Fire Point, para presionar a los ejecutivos a que terminaran rápidamente un modelo de mayor alcance, el FP-9, que según la empresa podría alcanzar Moscú. "Les dije: “¿Dónde está mi FP-9?", comentó Zelenski con una sonrisa. "Necesitamos el FP-9. Y el FP-9 estará (listo) este otoño boreal, estoy seguro". Zelenski señaló que la reciente oleada de incursiones de drones rusos y ataques híbridos en Europa constituía un intento de intimidar a las poblaciones europeas y de dividir el apoyo a Ucrania. Algunos líderes europeos estaban empezando a comprenderlo, señaló, y a endurecer su postura. Rusia afirma que tales acusaciones carecen de fundamento y son fruto de la histeria antirrusa. Tras las conversaciones mantenidas esta semana en Bruselas con funcionarios europeos, Ucrania había conseguido financiación para seguir adelante con los pedidos de drones que necesita para seguir luchando a principios de 2027, dijo Zelenski. Las autoridades ucranianas habían elaborado un plan junto con socios europeos para cubrir un agujero de 27.000 millones de dólares en el presupuesto de defensa de Kiev para este año. Los planes implican una combinación de la reasignación de los propios recursos presupuestarios de Ucrania, la ayuda bilateral y el uso de "créditos monetarios" procedentes de la parte correspondiente al próximo año de un préstamo de la UE de 90.000 millones de euros, explicó Zelenski.

item.title: Hermes shows airy knits and slit skirts in spring/summer 2027 collection
item.description: Hermès creative director Nadège Vanhée presented an airy spring/summer collection using gauzy fabrics at Paris Fashion Week on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Helen Reid
item.content:encoded: Hermès creative director Nadège Vanhée presented an airy spring/summer collection using gauzy fabrics at Paris Fashion Week on Saturday. Models wore loose-knit brown and black tops and dresses revealing bandeau tops underneath, or mesh dresses embroidered with panels of fine leather strips. Open latticework was also used on cream leather bucket handbags, and models mostly wore flat, minimalist leather sandals, with the occasional knee-high leather boot. Midi-length leather dresses and skirts were sliced into thigh-high strips, and trousers too had side zips open for ventilation. In a bright white show space inside the Garde Republicaine, the sprawling barracks of Paris' mounted gendarmes, guests including actors Sofia Vergara and Emmy Rossum fanned themselves on an unusually warm and sunny October day. The collection had splashes of colour, too, with a billowing parka in bright orange worn over a knit mini dress, and a zipped skirt in what Vanhée called sunflower yellow, paired with a matching high-collared jacket. Vanhée has been womenswear creative director since 2014 for Hermes, which caters to the ultra-wealthy and tightly controls access to its products, with years-long waiting lists for its most exclusive handbags. She will present the first haute couture collection for the brand in January. Hermes is one of many major luxury brands showing at Paris Fashion Week, which started on Monday and runs through October 6, with Chanel and Louis Vuitton runway shows still to come. The group is grappling with a slowdown in demand for luxury handbags and clothes and its shares are down 39% since the start of this year.

item.title: Ucrânia atacará refinarias russas em resposta à "nova doutrina" de ataques aéreos de Moscou
item.description: A Ucrânia intensificará os ataques às refinarias de petróleo russas em resposta a uma nova política de ataques aéreos de Moscou, destinada a forçar as pessoas a abandonarem Kiev e outras cidades, mas não terá como alvo civis, afirmou o presidente Volodymyr Zelenskiy.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: A Ucrânia intensificará os ataques às refinarias de petróleo russas em resposta a uma nova política de ataques aéreos de Moscou, destinada a forçar as pessoas a abandonarem Kiev e outras cidades, mas não terá como alvo civis, afirmou o presidente Volodymyr Zelenskiy. A inteligência ucraniana obteve documentos que mostram que o líder russo, Vladimir Putin, havia emitido uma "nova doutrina" de ataques militares contra uma gama muito mais ampla de alvos civis antes deste inverno, disse Zelenskiy. "Vimos os documentos e sabemos que eles permitem que ataquem infraestrutura... logística... estradas, escolas, hospitais, para pressionar as pessoas a deixarem a capital e outras cidades", disse Zelenskiy. "Esse é o objetivo da operação." O que impulsionou a mudança na política, disse Zelenskiy, foi o desejo de Putin de parecer forte em um momento em que suas forças armadas estavam perdendo terreno em uma região-chave da linha de frente e sofrendo um número maior de baixas. O Kremlin não se pronunciou no sábado. Mas, em comunicado instando cidadãos estrangeiros a deixarem Kiev, o Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Rússia afirmou que Moscou continuaria a atingir sistematicamente alvos no que chamou de ataques retaliatórios aos ataques ucranianos contra a Rússia nos últimos meses. Ambos os lados negam ter como alvo deliberadamente civis. CONTRATAQUE NO DONBAS Zelenskiy afirmou que uma contraofensiva ucraniana em andamento, de codinome “Vivaldi”, havia recapturado cerca de 140 km² (54 milhas quadradas) da região de Donbas, no leste da Ucrânia, que a Rússia afirma que deve controlar em sua totalidade como condição para qualquer acordo de paz. Nas últimas semanas, o governo do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, tem buscado retomar as negociações para pôr fim ao conflito que já dura quatro anos -- o mais sangrento da Europa desde a Segunda Guerra Mundial. No mês passado, o líder norte-americano instou a Ucrânia a evitar ataques a instalações petrolíferas russas, alegando que isso estava provocando uma alta nos preços globais do diesel. Mas Zelenskiy, falando enquanto sirenes de ataque aéreo soavam do lado de fora dos salões dourados dos escritórios presidenciais, disse não ter recebido nenhuma indicação da Rússia de que Putin estivesse interessado em negociações de paz ou em discutir um cessar-fogo em relação à infraestrutura energética. Na última semana, a capital ucraniana sofreu ataques persistentes de drones e mísseis russos contra ativos de energia e telecomunicações, além de infraestrutura rodoviária e ferroviária. Pela primeira vez, a Rússia atacou as pontes sobre o rio Dnipro que ligam o leste ao oeste de Kiev. Zelenskiy afirmou que a Ucrânia responderia à mudança de tática de Moscou, mas não retaliaria atacando infraestruturas civis indiscriminadamente.

item.title: ATP roundup: Carlos Alcaraz fights off 4 set points in Tokyo
item.description: Top-seeded Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz fought off four set points in the opener Saturday before rolling past Italy's Matteo Arnaldi to reach the Japan Open Tennis Championship quarterfinals in Tokyo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Top-seeded Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz fought off four set points in the opener Saturday before rolling past Italy's Matteo Arnaldi to reach the Japan Open Tennis Championship quarterfinals in Tokyo. Alcaraz completed the 7-6 (6), 6-1 victory in one hour and 46 minutes. He trailed 6-2 in the tiebreaker before winning six straight points, then carried the momentum into the second set by winning the first five games. Alcaraz's quarterfinal opponent will be Canadian Denis Shapovalov, a 7-5, 3-6, 6-4 winner against Chile's Alejandro Tabilo. Czech Jiri Lehecka also advanced in three sets against Frenchman Ugo Humbert and will take on Paraguayan qualifier Adolfo Daniel Vallejo, who saved all three break points in a 7-6 (6), 6-1 win over Italian Matteo Berrettini. The other quarterfinal matchups are France's Kyrian Jacquet vs. Spain's Jaume Munar, and No. 8 Valentin Vacherot of Monaco vs. France's Arthur Fils. China Open No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev of Germany moved into the quarterfinals in Beijing with a 6-0, 6-3 victory in 55 minutes against Chinese hopeful Juncheng Shang. Zverev struck nine aces, never faced a break point and converted four of his five break chances to set up a showdown with sixth-seeded Serbian Novak Djokovic. Djokovic is a six-time champion with a perfect 31-0 record in this tournament. Argentina's Francisco Cerundolo advanced with a 6-3, 6-3 win over eighth-seeded Czech Jakub Mensik. Up next is No. 3 seed Daniil Medvedev of Russia, who had 10 aces in a 6-4, 6-3 victory against Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff. No. 5 Alex de Minaur of Australia and Russia's Andrey Rublev will meet in the quarterfinals after posting three-set triumphs. Rublev outlasted compatriot Roman Safiullin 6-2, 3-6, 6-4, and de Minaur rallied past Frenchman Quentin Halys 3-6, 7-6 (5), 7-5 in two hours and 47 minutes. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brazil tame India in 4-0 friendly win
item.description: Samuel Lino scored his first two goals for Brazil as India's frantic effort to hold off the five-time world champions faded after a spirited start, allowing the visitors to cruise to a 4-0 win in a friendly on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Chiranjit Ojha
item.content:encoded: Samuel Lino scored his first two goals for Brazil as India's frantic effort to hold off the five-time world champions faded after a spirited start, allowing the visitors to cruise to a 4-0 win in a friendly on Saturday. Chelsea winger Estevao scored Brazil's first goal and assisted Pedro before Lino netted a second-half brace, helping Carlo Ancelotti's side conclude their tour of Australia and India with two wins and a draw. Ancelotti, who has experimented with the squad throughout the three friendlies, made eight changes from Tuesday's 4-2 win over Australia, retaining only Vinicius Jr, Danilo and Gabriel Bontempo. India's strategy of leaving Vinicius unmarked on the left and trapping him offside had some early success as they combined their defenders with a low midfield to hold Brazil off, and targeted lone forward Manvir Singh with long balls. But Estevao delivered the breakthrough in the 28th minute, cutting in from the right to dispatch a left-footer at the near post, before setting up Brazil's second with a defence-splitting pass for Pedro to finish. Pedro set up Samuel Lino for the third goal near the hour mark, before the 26-year-old Flamengo winger dribbled past two defenders to make it 4-0 just before fulltime, as the crowd of 51,000 at the Salt Lake Stadium [USN:L6N45O0MC TEXT:"cheered the visitors"] as vocally as their own country. India, ranked 138th in the world, were left ruing their missed chances as Manvir and Ryan Williams failed to net a consolation goal, extending their winless streak to six matches.

item.title: Ukraine will hit Russian refineries in response to Moscow's 'new doctrine' of airstrikes, Zelenskiy says
item.description: Ukrainian intelligence has documents showing that Vladimir Putin called for military attacks on a much broader range of civilian targets ahead of this winter, Zelenskiy told Reuters in an interview.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: Ukraine will double down on attacking Russian oil refineries in response to a new policy of airstrikes by Moscow designed to [USN:L8N44V1KC TEXT:"force people to abandon Kyiv"] and other cities, but will not target civilians, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said. Ukraine's intelligence services has obtained documents showing that Russian leader Vladimir Putin had issued a "new doctrine" of military attacks on a much broader range of civilian targets ahead of this winter, Zelenskiy said. "We saw documents and we know that they allow them to attack infrastructure, logistics, and especially to attack in the cities, in the villages, everywhere, roads, schools, hospitals," Zelenskiy told Reuters in an interview. "To pressure people to leave the capital, leave different cities: this is the goal of the operation." Driving the shift in policy, Zelenskiy said, was Putin's desire to appear strong at a time when his military was losing ground in a key frontline region and sustaining higher levels of casualties. The Kremlin was not available to comment on Saturday. But in a statement [USN:L1N45P03K TEXT:"urging foreign nationals to leave Kyiv"], the Russian Foreign Ministry said Moscow would continue to systematically hit targets in what it said were retaliatory strikes for Ukrainian attacks on Russia in recent months. Both sides deny deliberately targeting civilians. COUNTEROFFENSIVE IN DONBAS Zelenskiy said a successful Ukrainian counteroffensive, code-named "Vivaldi", had recaptured around 140 sq km (54 sq miles) of Ukrain's eastern Donbas region and was still ongoing. Russia has said it must control Donbas in its entirety as a condition for any peace deal. In recent weeks, US President Donald Trump's administration has sought to revive talks to end the four-year-old conflict – Europe's bloodiest since World War Two. The US leader last month urged Ukraine [USN:L1N45503J TEXT:"to refrain from hitting Russian oil installations"], saying that was sending global diesel prices surging. But Zelenskiy, speaking as air raid sirens blared outside the gilded halls of the presidential offices, said he had received no indications from Russia that Putin was interested in peace talks, or discussing a ceasefire on energy infrastructure. Over the past week, the Ukrainian capital has come under persistent attack by Russian drones and missiles targeting energy and telecoms assets, road and rail infrastructure. For the first time, Russia has [USN:L1N45P00Z TEXT:"targeted the bridges"] across the Dnipro river connecting east and west Kyiv. Zelenskiy said Ukraine would react to the change in tactics by Moscow, but would not target civilian infrastructure indiscriminately. "We have to respond in any way (we can). With their attacks on our energy, we have to respond on their energy. First of all, oil refiners etc: what gives money to them for this war," Zelenskiy said in English. "But we will not respond, of course, just like them, on any civilian objects." SUPPORT FROM EUROPE After the Trump administration invited Putin [USN:L6N45F16H TEXT:"to attend a G20 summit in Miami"] in December and discussed business deals with Russian envoys, Zelenskiy urged Washington not to normalise relations with Russia before ensuring a return to peace. Zelenskiy said he would be happy to meet Putin for peace talks at the G20, but he warned the US not to believe in "illusions" that Russia would simply end hostilities if it gained control of Donbas. "It's not fair just to normalise," said Zelenskiy, dressed in his trademark black T-shirt and military-style jacket. Any resumption of economic and diplomatic ties with the West had to be in return for Russia ending hostilities, he said: "Because peace is more important than any kind of economy." While the US has proposed a resumption of trilateral talks in the coming weeks in the UAE, Zelenskiy noted that an exact date and location for the technical-level conversations had still not been set. Ukrainian officials warn that Russia has stockpiled hundreds of ballistic missiles ahead of an expected winter onslaught against electricity and water infrastructure. Last winter, the worst of the war, Russian strikes left swathes of the country without electricity and heating for days at a time. Since the summer, Moscow has also begun launching dozens of fast and relatively cheap jet-powered Shahed drones a day at Ukraine, whose air defence teams have struggled to cope because their interceptor drones were too slow to catch them. Zelenskiy said Ukraine had been forced to rely heavily on its fighter aircraft – F-16s and MiGs – to down around 60% of the Russian jet-powered drones, but supplies of 20 mm ammunition for the planes were running low. Kyiv was urgently working on other solutions – including boosting its electronic jamming capabilities, he said. In the second half of October, it would receive the first shipment of small, cheap air defence missiles capable of hitting the new Shaheds. Last week, Zelenskiy said Ukraine was developing five models of new interceptor drones capable of downing the jet Shaheds. Fresh from a meeting with his defence chiefs, he said tests on two of those models showed a modest success rate of around 30%. "We'll have to scale it," he said. "I hope that with all these things, with all these elements, we'll find a way." BALLISTIC THREAT Ukraine announced the first combat use this week of its own domestically made ballistic missile, the FP-7, which has a range of around 250 km (155 miles). Zelenskiy said he had called the manufacturer Fire Point to pressure executives to finish a longer-range model, the FP-9, which the company has said could hit Moscow. "I said to them, where is my FP-9?" said Zelenskiy, with a grin. "We need the FP-9. And the FP-9 will be (ready) this autumn, I'm sure." Zelenskiy said a recent spate of Russian drone incursions and hybrid attacks in Europe were an effort to intimidate European populations and to undermine support for Ukraine. Some European leaders were starting to understand this, he said, and toughen their position. Russia says such accusations are baseless and the result of anti-Russian hysteria. After talks with European officials in Brussels this week, Ukraine had unlocked funding to order the drones that it needs to keep fighting at the start of 2027, Zelenskiy said. Ukrainian officials had worked on plans with European partners to plug a $27 billion hole in Kyiv's defence budget this year. The plans involve a combination of the reallocation of Ukraine's own budget resources, bilateral assistance and using "money credits" from next year's portion of a €90 billion EU loan, Zelenskiy said. "We will close this (gap). I think this is absolutely a big success for our country," he said.

Netherlands coach Xavi joins critics of new-look international window

FAST

Oct 3 : Netherlands coach Xavi Hernandez has joined the criticism of the new-look expanded international calendar, saying four Nations League matches in 11 days are filled with peril. Instead of two international games across nine days in each of September and October, FIFA has this year combined the two international windows into one with four match days, making for an intense programme. “This schedule is not good. Not for the national teams and not for the clubs that release their players and sometimes see them return injured,” Xavi told a press conference- on Saturday. The Dutch have 23 fit players for the Group A2 game against Serbia in Eindhoven on Sunday, with Brian Brobbey, Lutsharel Geertruida, Cody Gakpo and Jan Paul van Hecke all injured in their last three games and back at their clubs.

“Scheduling such a packed calendar three months after the World Cup is asking for trouble,” Xavi added. “You also have training, travelling, recovering from matches and things like that. It’s very strange to schedule an international window like this at this stage of the season.” Spaniard Xavi, who was appointed Netherlands coach in August, suggested that authorities review the situation. “I would rather see us play two internationals," he said. "That would be better for everyone. But as far as I know, it was decided a long time ago that we will also have a block of four matches at this stage next year.” NEW INTERNATIONAL WINDOW POSES CHALLENGE The longer international window was always going to be a challenge for national team coaches, without any experience of how to handle the extra workload. Germany’s new coach Juergen Klopp called up 44 players in two separate squads, although the team's results have been mixed. “The shifts in training, work style, and play style between the national team and club inherently create certain risks. This format only heightens those risks rather than alleviating them,” England manager Thomas Tuchel said this week. Spain's World Cup-winning coach Luis de la Fuente aired his opinion last month: "I don't like the new format; I prefer the old one. It gave you more rest. In my opinion, it took better care of the players' health,” he said. The next three international windows in November, March, and June will be the usual nine-day period with two match days, but FIFA has scheduled a combined September/October window of 16 days for the next four years, through to 2030.

(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Ed Osmond)

item.title: ShinyHunters hacker in FBI data theft detained in Jordan, cooperating with bureau, sources say
item.description: A suspected member of the ShinyHunters hacking group, which says it stole data on every FBI employee, was detained in Jordan this week and is cooperating with the FBI, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Jana Winter, Raphael Satter, A.J. Vicens
item.content:encoded: A suspected member of the ShinyHunters hacking group, which says it stole data on every FBI employee, was detained in Jordan this week and is cooperating with the FBI, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters. Saif al-Din Khader was detained by Jordanian authorities, the three sources said. Two of them said he was brought into custody on Tuesday. Reuters could not immediately determine the circumstances of Khader’s detention or where he is being held. Two sources said that he is helping the FBI and global law enforcement locate the other hackers in the group. The FBI declined to comment on any specific arrest or activity abroad but said that the bureau "continues to aggressively investigate the recent cyber incident allegedly involving ShinyHunters, having already worked with partners to arrest multiple subjects — and we will spare no resource in bringing each of the responsible individuals to justice." Reuters’ attempts to reach Khader and members of his family over the past week and a half have been unsuccessful. The detention of Khader — whose alleged hacker nickname is Rey — is the latest twist in the case of ShinyHunters. The prolific cyber extortion group, which has a long history of targeting major corporations around the world, is believed by experts to consist mainly of young, English-speaking hackers focused on data theft and extortion. Their theft of what they claim are mountains of data on every single FBI employee has drawn comparisons to the allegedly Chinese-linked intrusion at the US Office of Personnel Management in 2015, which compromised sensitive details on millions of Americans who had been vetted for security clearances. SENSITIVE INFORMATION A Reuters [USN:L6N45F0ZI TEXT:"analysis"] of a sample of the data shared by ShinyHunters revealed that the data contained extensive personally identifiable information of FBI employees, sensitive job role information, and psychiatric and medical information. Khader's cooperation with investigators could be critical to helping contain -- or at least understand -- the damage. One source said he was walking investigators through his electronic devices and digital correspondence to help the FBI locate his cohorts. "His cooperation is critical to ongoing efforts to arrest these hackers," the source told Reuters. There have been hints for days that ShinyHunters was experiencing disruption following the announcement of its break-in at the FBI. Beginning on Tuesday, Reuters was unable to reach ShinyHunters through the online account it previously used to communicate with journalists. Then, on Wednesday, the group’s dark web site, where it had previously posted threats to the FBI, [USN:L6N45M1CE TEXT:"disappeared"]. FBI Director Kash Patel had been hinting at more arrests following [USN:S8N42N0JB TEXT:"the announcement"] that another alleged ShinyHunters member, Pepijn van der Stap, had been detained in the Netherlands. “FBI teams are working new leads RIGHT NOW,” Patel said on Wednesday in a message posted to X. “More arrests are on the table.” The operators of a ShinyHunters-linked email address did not respond to a request for comment on Friday. The operators of that email account previously told Reuters that the group’s site had gone offline due to sabotage from rivals and "disruption due to an unrelated incident." The group had previously struck a defiant note, saying on September 22 that it had hacked the FBI in retaliation over an advisory that accused ShinyHunters of making "exaggerated claims of access" to extort victims for money. It gave the FBI a week to withdraw the advisory. But in the most recent email to Reuters, the operators struck a conciliatory tone, saying that “we want no further escalation” with the FBI. The operators said Reuters could interpret their message as meaning, “ShinyHunters backing down completely.” KHADER'S IDENTITY LONG KNOWN Khader’s identity, and his alleged connection to ShinyHunters, have long been known to security researchers. Last year, the independent journalist Brian Krebs reported that Khader was a key member of Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters, an umbrella group of hackers that included ShinyHunters. Krebs, who said he spoke to Khader over Signal, quoted the teenager as saying he had quit the world of data breaches and extortion and was cooperating with law enforcement. But ShinyHunters continued its hacking spree into 2026, claiming credit for break-ins at [USN:L6N40W1A9 TEXT:"video game developer Rockstar Games"], the maker of "Grand Theft Auto," and a May intrusion involving [USN:L6N41P0Z6 TEXT:"education tool Canvas"] that caused widespread disruption [USN:L6N41L0UT TEXT:"across US schools"]. Law enforcement agencies around the world, including in the United States, have struggled to arrest and prosecute members of related groups such as Lapsus$ or Scattered Spider, [USN:L1N3CE2RM TEXT:"Reuters has previously reported"]. Sources told Reuters that the difficulty stems from the hackers’ young ages, which can make prosecutions complex, or because the groups they belong to are so chaotic and informal, or because victims of their extortion attempts often decline to help investigators.

item.title: Fake Jobs Put Job Seekers at Risk of Identity Theft

item.title: OF Aaron Judge (calf) left off Yankees' ALDS roster
item.description: Captain Aaron Judge was left off the New York Yankees' roster for their American League Division Series against the Tampa Bay Rays.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Captain Aaron Judge was left off the New York Yankees' roster for their American League Division Series against the Tampa Bay Rays. The Yankees revealed their 26-man roster for the best-of-five series on Saturday morning, with Game 1 set for 6:38 p.m. ET in St. Petersburg, Fla. Judge, 34, has not played since Sept. 16 with a strained right calf. The three-time AL MVP landed on the injured list three days later and missed the Yankees' two-game wild-card sweep against the rival Boston Red Sox earlier this week. "Ultimately, I obviously decided keeping (Judge off the roster) was the best thing," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "Again, I feel like he's getting close, but I feel like for us to get a version of Aaron back and to win a World Series, I feel like this week's important for him to continue to work towards getting back. He just started running. He's hit now a couple of days. So I think another several days of doing that and building some endurance, I think, is important. "Understanding entirely that we're guaranteed nothing. (If) we don't play well, next week we're home and we don't get it. But I feel like for us to get a good version of Aaron, this was the right thing to do." Judge faced live pitching for the first time since the injury on Monday, was running in the outfield on Tuesday and took batting practice on Wednesday and Thursday. The outfielder participated in workouts on Friday at the Yankees' minor league facility in Tampa and also at Tropicana Field. Judge has voiced his determination to return in the postseason, but the team ultimately decided to move forward without him against Tampa Bay. Trent Grisham, Spencer Jones, Heliot Ramos and Giancarlo Stanton are the outfielders on the ALDS roster set to face the Rays. Boone said Stanton is only available for pinch-hitting. Stanton hasn't played in a game since April 24. "If there's any time to erase a bad year, it's in October," Stanton said. "It's the biggest opportunity to show out for the city and do what we can do." Cody Bellinger and Jose Caballero, who can play in both the infield and outfield, are listed as utility players. Judge largely was ineffective before the calf injury, batting .174 (4-for-23) with a homer and three RBIs in seven games after his Sept. 8 return from the injured list. He had missed more than three months with a fractured rib. "Yeah, but it's more about the endurance, more about the going out there and playing a baseball game for three hours," Boone said. "I mean, he hasn't done anything really for a couple weeks in that regard. That's the challenge of all this." In 66 games overall this year, Judge batted .241 with a .360 on-base percentage, a .511 slugging percentage, 18 homers and 41 RBIs. That is the fewest number of games Judge has played since his 2016 debut season, not including the 2020 pandemic campaign. An eight-time All-Star, Judge still is looking for his first World Series championship. He is a career .236 hitter in the postseason with 17 home runs and 41 RBIs in 65 games. --Field Level Media

item.title: Egypt Flagged Hamas Threat Before Oct. 7

item.title: OpenAI safety employee quits, urges nuclear-level safeguards for AI risks
item.description: Former OpenAI safety employee David Robinson has warned that AI companies need stronger safeguards as artificial intelligence capabilities advance ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: An OpenAI employee focused on AI safety has quit the company and warned that top artificial intelligence firms aren’t doing enough to mitigate the technology’s risks, joining a growing chorus of employees raising alarms from within the industry.  David Robinson, who previously led transparency work on OpenAI’s safety team, wrote in an essay for The Atlantic that the ChatGPT maker “has thrived by trial and error.” However, he said the stakes of the inevitable failures that come from that approach are growing along with the technology’s capabilities, citing OpenAI’s failure to prevent its AI from going rogue during testing. “My former colleagues are smart, work hard, and try to make good choices,” Robinson wrote in the essay. “But as the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the level of care that I believe is needed.” What’s required, he added, is “something much closer to perfection the first time.” A number of employees across the top AI companies in recent weeks have warned about the potential catastrophic risks from artificial intelligence. Some have gone so far as to say there’s a chance the technology could one day wipe out the human race.  Against that backdrop, Anthropic PBC Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei called for slowing down the pace of developing the most cutting-edge models, and said his company would bring on third-party evaluators to help vet and safeguard the technology. Others in the industry, including OpenAI’s Sam Altman, have publicly endorsed Amodei’s plan.  In his essay, Robinson said AI firms should be run more like nuclear power plants, “with layers of redundancy and careful, time-consuming planning, so that the occasional and inevitable human error does not open a door to disaster.” At the moment, he said, “AI companies don’t know how — but other people do.” (Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: Why Philosophers Are Worried About AI
item.description: Debate over artificial intelligence has largely focused on whether machines could become too powerful. Harvard philosopher Michael Sandel argues that a more immediate question is whether AI changes humans themselves: weakening authentic connection, independent thought and the ways people understand meaning and purpose. Universities are already confronting that challenge as students increasingly use AI to learn and communicate, while Vanderbilt University Chairman Daniel Diermeier argues that technological fluency must be paired with the ability to think independently. item.title: Respaldo de Larry Ellison preocupa a inversionistas por el alto endeudamiento de Paramount y Oracle
item.description: El magnate apyoya la adquisición de Warner Bros. por parte de Paramount —liderada por su hijo David— a través de un fideicomiso familiar y se comprometió a tomar las medidas necesarias para ayudar a r ...
item.dc:creator: Davide Barbuscia
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg — A medida que Paramount Skydance Corp. y Oracle Corp. se sitúan entre las empresas más endeudadas de Estados Unidos, sus vínculos con una misma persona —el multimillonario Larry Ellison— están empezando a generar inquietud en Wall Street. Muchos inversionistas han dado por hecho que Ellison intervendría para respaldar a Paramount si esta se viera en dificultades financieras tras haber contraído esta semana una deuda adicional de US$52.000 millones para financiar la adquisición de Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. Sin embargo, dado que gran parte de la fortuna de la familia Ellison está vinculada a las acciones de Oracle —mientras la empresa lleva a cabo su propia expansión en inteligencia artificial, que requiere una gran inversión de capital—, existe la preocupación de que el valor de esa red de seguridad pueda verse sometido a presión precisamente cuando Paramount más la necesita. Esas preocupaciones ya se están reflejando en el mercado, según afirman los gestores de fondos. El costo de asegurar la deuda de ambas empresas frente al impago se ha equiparado y evoluciona cada vez más al unísono, una señal de que los inversionistas están empezando a considerar que los dos créditos están interrelacionados. Se trata de otro factor que los prestamistas deben tener en cuenta a la hora de evaluar la creciente deuda y el riesgo de ejecución de las empresas, según Campe Goodman, gestor de carteras de Wellington Management Co. “Hay que tener en cuenta el riesgo total asociado a Larry Ellison”, afirmó Goodman, añadiendo que los inversores deberían considerar a Oracle y Paramount como inversiones relacionadas, en lugar de como créditos completamente independientes. “Probablemente convenga tener en cuenta la exposición a ambas”. Los representantes de Paramount y Oracle no respondieron a las solicitudes de comentarios. Los intentos de contactar con Ellison a través de su fundación tampoco obtuvieron respuesta. Ellison, de 82 años, respalda la adquisición de Warner Bros. por parte de Paramount —liderada por su hijo David— a través de un fideicomiso familiar que garantizó una parte significativa de los aproximadamente US$47.000 millones de financiación mediante capital propio destinados a la operación. Sin embargo, su apoyo va más allá de la propia adquisición. Mientras Paramount se esforzaba por tranquilizar a las agencias de calificación sobre la carga de deuda que soportaría la empresa fusionada, la familia Ellison se comprometió a tomar todas las medidas necesarias para ayudar a reducir el apalancamiento en los próximos años —un compromiso que las agencias de calificación e inversores interpretaron como una promesa tácita de inyectar capital adicional en caso de necesidad—. Esto hace que la capacidad de Ellison para cumplir su compromiso sea un factor clave para los tenedores de deuda. Hace apenas un año, las acciones de Oracle se dispararon hasta alcanzar un máximo histórico en medio del creciente optimismo en torno a la inteligencia artificial, lo que le convirtió brevemente en la persona más rica del mundo. Desde entonces, su fortuna se ha desplomado en casi US$200.000 millones —más que la de cualquier otra persona del mundo, según el Índice de Multimillonarios de Bloomberg—. Para que quede claro, su patrimonio sigue ascendiendo a unos US$192.000 millones de dólares, lo suficiente para situarlo entre las diez personas más ricas. Pero este brusco cambio de tendencia pone de manifiesto hasta qué punto su fortuna puede fluctuar en función de la cotización de las acciones de Oracle. El mes pasado, Ellison canceló un plan para vender acciones de la empresa por valor de miles de millones de dólares, en la que aún posee una participación de aproximadamente el 40%. También reveló que había aumentado el número de acciones pignoradas como garantía de sus préstamos personales. “Los negocios no podrían ser más diferentes, pero el mercado está empezando a relacionarlos a través de un patrocinador común”, afirmó Steven Schweitzer, gestor de carteras de Advent Capital Management. “Parte de la trayectoria crediticia de Paramount está ligada a la confianza en la trayectoria de Oracle, ya que la solidez financiera de Larry Ellison respalda a ambas”. El paquete de financiación de Paramount, que se cerró el miércoles, incluía US$30.000 millones en bonos con calificación de inversión, el equivalente a US$12.400 millones en bonos de alto riesgo y US$9.460 millones en préstamos. Según participantes del mercado, en las conversaciones previas a la venta, los inversores que se planteaban participar debatían activamente qué peso dar al compromiso de la familia Ellison. “La cuestión es que, si a Paramount no le va bien y las acciones de Oracle caen mucho, se sigue teniendo la misma base de activos, y ahí es donde existe una posible interrelación”, afirmó Jawad Hussain, analista de S&P Global Ratings. Esto podría llevar al mercado a preguntarse: “¿Podría afectar a la capacidad de los Ellison para respaldar los activos de Paramount, que necesita reducir su apalancamiento?“. Por su parte, Oracle casi ha duplicado su deuda a largo plazo hasta superar los US$160.000 millones de dólares en los últimos dos años, a medida que la empresa se reinventa como proveedora de potencia informática para aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial. Actualmente figura como el quinto mayor emisor de deuda en el mercado de bonos corporativos de EE. UU., según datos del índice de Bloomberg. En julio, S&P rebajó la calificación de Oracle a BBB-, el nivel más bajo dentro del grado de inversión, ya que el elevado gasto empujó el flujo de caja libre a un territorio profundamente negativo. El mes pasado rebajó la calificación crediticia de Paramount como emisor a BB, dos escalones por debajo del grado de inversión, ante las expectativas de un mayor apalancamiento tras la adquisición de Warner Bros. El aumento del gasto de Oracle, impulsado por la deuda, también ha inquietado a los inversionistas en renta variable, eclipsando el sólido crecimiento de su división de computación en la nube y provocando una caída de más del 50% en el precio de sus acciones durante el último año. Brett Kozlowski, gestor de carteras de GW&K Investment Management, señaló que el riesgo es recíproco tanto para los tenedores de deuda de Paramount como para los de Oracle. “Existe el riesgo para la deuda de Oracle de que, si la fusión entre Paramount y WBD no se lleva a cabo según lo previsto, el respaldo de la familia Ellison pueda vincular ambos créditos en mayor medida de lo que se refleja en los precios”, señaló por correo electrónico. “Esto crea la posibilidad de una convergencia entre ambos créditos y beneficia a Paramount frente a Oracle, ya que la deuda de Paramount, más débil, obtendría el apoyo potencial del balance de Oracle, más sólido”. --Con la colaboración de Anders Melin y David Scheer. item.title: US Coast Guard searches for medical aircraft carrying six from Bermuda to Boston
item.description: A medical transfer aircraft carrying six people was reported missing on a flight from Bermuda to Boston, the US Coast Guard said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Sheila Dang
item.content:encoded: A medical transfer aircraft carrying six people was reported missing on a flight from Bermuda to Boston, the US Coast Guard said on Saturday. The Federal Aviation Administration told the Coast Guard early on Saturday that it had lost contact with the plane, a Gulfstream jet, a Coast Guard spokesperson said by email. Four Canadians are on the plane, Canadian Minister of Transport Steven MacKinnon said on X. "We are closely monitoring the situation and are working with the relevant authorities as search and rescue efforts continue," he wrote. The aircraft, registered to Latitude Air Ambulance, departed Bermuda at 12:41 a.m. local time, according to data from flight tracking website FlightAware. The plane was flying at 24,000 feet (7,300 metres) for much of the flight before descending 13,000 feet in about two minutes shortly before flight controllers lost contact, data showed. Local TV station Boston 25 posted an audio clip from Boston Logan International Airport in which an air traffic controller can be heard asking the Gulfstream pilot, "You said you're coming in blind? Is that what you said?" The controller then asked whether the plane was declaring an emergency. No response was heard. Latitude is based in Ontario, Canada, and provides medical evacuation services. The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Coast Guard said it dispatched air and surface crews to search for the plane near Nantucket, an island community south of mainland Massachusetts. The Bermuda government is in contact with US authorities and families of the passengers, Bermuda Premier David Burt wrote in a statement posted on Instagram. "We are praying that all six people will be found safe," he wrote. Weather conditions in Nantucket were clear as of Saturday afternoon, according to AccuWeather.

item.title: Portugal prosecutors probe legality of US use of Lajes base in Iran war
item.description: A longstanding agreement with the US allows it to use the Azores air base without prior authorization during peacetime.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Portuguese prosecutors said on Saturday they had opened a probe into the legality of the centre-right government's authorisation of the United States' use of the Lajes Air Base in the Azores during the Iran conflict, following a complaint by an opposition party. A longstanding agreement with the US allows Washington to use the base without prior authorisation during peacetime, but requires Portugal to give approval once hostilities begin. Portugal, unlike neighbouring Spain, [USN:L8N3ZS22H TEXT:"authorised several US transit flights"] through the Lajes air base, a decision that drew criticism from left-wing opposition parties and triggered a political debate over Lisbon's role in operations linked to the conflict with Iran. In a statement, the Prosecutor General's Office said "the probe was opened following a complaint filed by members of the Left Bloc party," without providing further details. Portugal's Foreign Ministry declined to comment. The Left Bloc asked prosecutors in April to investigate the US use of the Lajes base, arguing it amounted to a "gross violation of international law." However, Foreign Minister Paulo Rangel has said Portugal was not involved in the conflict and that the use of the Lajes base complied with international law, having been authorised only after assurances from Washington that any operation would be defensive, necessary and proportionate, and limited to military targets. Portugal's prosecutors are bound by the principle of legality, requiring them to investigate alleged wrongdoing when there are sufficient grounds to do so, unlike in some jurisdictions where prosecutors have broader discretion to decide whether a case should proceed. The Lajes base, located in Portugal's Atlantic Azores archipelago, is a strategic transit hub for US forces under a bilateral defence treaty dating back to 1951 and hosts the 65th Air Base Wing of the US Air Force, providing support for US, NATO and allied operations.

item.title: Tens of thousands protest across Spain over housing crisis
item.description: Anger swelled over the eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her apartment in Madrid.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Spanish police arrested three members of a far-right group and fired rubber bullets on Saturday night in Madrid after tens of thousands had marched across the country to demand action to tackle a housing crisis. Far-right activists, some of whom performed Nazi salutes, tried to reach demonstrators camped out in the Puerta del Sol, a central square in the Spanish capital, to protest the housing crisis, the Spanish government said. Earlier, some demonstrators waved posters calling for a general strike after the measures drawn up to address mass anger over the eviction of an 87-year-old woman in Madrid, and other housing issues, were [USN:L8N45F0PQ TEXT:"rejected"] in parliament on Friday. "It's a shame," said Nando de Anguulo, 26, who joined Saturday's protest in Madrid. "It only proves that it is us, the people, who have to adapt to the political parties, and not the politicians to what the people want, and this can't go on like that." Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez might call a snap election for November after the legislation failed to pass and would be watching the strength of Saturday's protests before deciding, Spanish media reported on Friday. Sanchez's office declined to comment on the reports. In the southeastern city of Valencia, demonstrators clashed with police who fired rubber bullets and tear gas to break up protests. About 30 protesters entered the City of Arts and Sciences, a landmark cultural complex, before police ousted them. Other demonstrations in 50 Spanish cities were peaceful. Valeria Racu, spokesperson for the Tenants Union, told reporters in Madrid that a general strike would be called after talks with labour unions. About 70,000 protesters took part in Saturday's demonstration in Madrid, the Spanish government said. Protests planned in Barcelona and the nearby city of Hospitalet de Llobregat were called off because of heavy rain.
